exact_bilingual_spans.text: الأول : أنه نهر في الجنة ; رواه البخاري عن أنس والترمذي أيضا وقد ذكرناه في كتاب التذكرة .
**The First:** It is a river in Paradise. Al-Bukhari reported it from Anas, and al-Tirmidhi likewise, and we have mentioned it in the Book of Remembrance.

وروى الترمذي أيضا عن ابن عمر قال : قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - : الكوثر : نهر في الجنة ، حافتاه من ذهب ، ومجراه على الدر والياقوت ، تربته أطيب من المسك ، وماؤه أحلى من العسل وأبيض من الثلج . هذا حديث حسن صحيح .

Al-Tirmidhi also reported from Ibn Umar, who said the Messenger of God, may God's prayers and peace be upon him, said: "Al-Kawthar is a river in Paradise. Its banks are of gold, its bed flows with pearls and rubies, its soil is more fragrant than musk, its water is sweeter than honey and whiter than snow." This is a sound, authentic hadith.

voice_decomposition.supported_content: The first of sixteen interpretations identifies al-Kawthar as a river in Paradise.
voice_decomposition.boundary: Do not treat al-Qurtubi as the originator of the prophetic reports he cites.

voice_decomposition.voice: Anas transmits a prophetic report; al-Qurtubi cites al-Bukhari and al-Tirmidhi
voice_decomposition.supported_content: Anas-linked collection reports identify the paradisal river as al-Kawthar and describe pearl-domed banks; al-Tirmidhi 3360 also mentions musk soil.
voice_decomposition.boundary: The stored al-Qurtubi span gives collection and Companion citations but does not quote the Anas wording or its full isnad. Do not attach the Ibn Umar gold/rubies/honey/snow details to Anas.

voice_decomposition.voice: Ibn Umar transmits from the Prophet; al-Tirmidhi is the cited collector
voice_decomposition.supported_content: Gold banks, pearls and rubies, musk-like soil, honey-like sweetness and snow-like whiteness belong to the quoted Ibn Umar report.
voice_decomposition.boundary: Keep these descriptors scoped to the Ibn Umar quotation.

voice_decomposition.supported_content: The Arabic technical grading is hasan sahih.
voice_decomposition.boundary: This is al-Tirmidhi's quoted grading, not a new authentication judgment by al-Qurtubi. English 'sound, authentic' is a loose rendering; retain the Arabic technical label in structured data.

collection_specific_routes.content_boundary: River with hollow pearl domes; identified to the Prophet as al-Kawthar.
collection_specific_routes.route_scope: External collection-specific route; not present in full in the stored al-Qurtubi row and not yet eligible for persistence as an al-Qurtubi transmission route.

collection_specific_routes.content_boundary: River with pearl tents, angel identifies it as al-Kawthar, musk soil; followed by Sidrat al-Muntaha material.
collection_specific_routes.route_scope: External collection-specific route; the stored al-Qurtubi row cites Tirmidhi but omits the isnad and quoted Anas text.

collection_specific_routes.content_boundary: Gold banks; pearls and rubies; musk; honey; snow; followed by al-Tirmidhi's hasan sahih grading.
collection_specific_routes.route_scope: Externally attested route matching the stored quotation; still not a license to infer independence or authentication beyond the cited collection statement.

fidelity_findings.external_english_translation_variant: One modern English witness renders the final comparison as milk although the Arabic and stored English read snow; Arabic الثلج controls.

next_target.task: Separate Ata's cistern interpretation from the Anas report quoted from Sahih Muslim, preserving the distinction between commentator interpretation, prophetic quotation and al-Qurtubi's later synthesis of river/cistern terminology.
